name: Forensics
summary: Acquisition and analysis tools for disk, memory, file and artifact forensics
description: A digital-forensics kit for authorized incident response and investigation: imaging and write-safe acquisition, filesystem and deleted-file analysis, carving, memory and registry artifacts, malware triage and anti-virus scanning. Use these on evidence you are authorized to examine, and keep an auditable chain of custody.

tools.name: The Sleuth Kit
tools.summary: Command-line tools for volume and filesystem forensic analysis
tools.notes: Provides fls, icat, mmls, fsstat and more; Autopsy is a graphical front end for the same engine.

tools.name: Autopsy
tools.summary: Web front end to The Sleuth Kit for case-based investigation
tools.notes: Starts a local web server you then open in a browser; this is the classic Perl Autopsy, not the separate Windows Autopsy product.

tools.name: Guymager
tools.summary: Graphical forensic disk imaging tool (dd, EWF, AFF)
tools.notes: Acquiring a device needs root; launch it from a privileged session or via its polkit integration.

tools.name: dc3dd
tools.summary: Patched dd with hashing and logging for forensic imaging

tools.name: libewf tools
tools.summary: Acquire and read Expert Witness Format (E01) evidence images

tools.name: TestDisk and PhotoRec
tools.summary: Recover lost partitions and carve files from media

tools.name: Foremost
tools.summary: Carve files from images based on headers and footers

tools.name: Scalpel
tools.summary: Fast, filesystem-independent file carver

tools.name: Binwalk
tools.summary: Analyse and extract embedded data from firmware and blobs

tools.name: extundelete
tools.summary: Recover deleted files from ext3 and ext4 filesystems

tools.name: GNU ddrescue
tools.summary: Copy data from failing drives, retrying bad areas last
tools.notes: Package gddrescue ships the ddrescue command (not to be confused with dd_rescue).

tools.name: YARA
tools.summary: Match files and processes against pattern rules for malware triage

tools.name: ClamAV
tools.summary: Open-source antivirus engine and command-line scanner

tools.name: chkrootkit
tools.summary: Check a system or mounted image for signs of a rootkit

tools.name: ssdeep
tools.summary: Compute and compare fuzzy (context-triggered) hashes

tools.name: hashdeep
tools.summary: Recursively hash files and audit sets of known hashes

tools.name: ExifTool
tools.summary: Read and write metadata in images, documents and media

tools.name: RegRipper
tools.summary: Extract forensic artifacts from Windows registry hives

tools.name: python-evtx
tools.summary: Parse Windows Event Log (EVTX) files into XML

tools.name: Plaso
tools.summary: Build a super-timeline from many forensic artifact sources
tools.notes: Debian prefixes the tools: plaso-log2timeline builds the timeline and plaso-psort post-processes it.

tools.name: dcfldd
tools.summary: Enhanced dd with on-the-fly hashing for imaging

tools.name: wxHexEditor
tools.summary: Hex editor that handles very large files and devices

external.name: Volatility 3
external.summary: Memory-forensics framework for analysing RAM captures
external.license: VSL (Volatility Software License, BSD-style); not currently in Debian trixie.

why.text: Volatility 3 is free software but is not packaged in Debian trixie; it is distributed on PyPI and GitHub.

how.text: Install into an isolated environment with pipx (pipx install volatility3), or run it from the official git checkout.

external.name: bulk_extractor
external.summary: Scan disk images for emails, URLs and other features
external.license: MIT/public-domain (open source); not currently in Debian trixie.

why.text: bulk_extractor is maintained on GitHub and is not in Debian trixie.

how.text: Build from the official source release with the standard autotools steps; its dependencies are in Debian.

external.name: Chainsaw
external.summary: Fast triage of Windows event logs with Sigma support
external.license: GPL-3.0 (open source); not packaged in Debian.

why.text: Chainsaw is a Rust tool distributed as release binaries outside Debian.

how.text: Download the official release binary for Linux, or build with 'cargo install chainsaw'.

external.name: Hayabusa
external.summary: Windows event-log timeline and threat hunting
external.license: AGPL-3.0 (open source); not packaged in Debian.

why.text: Hayabusa is a Rust tool distributed as release archives outside Debian.

how.text: Download the official release archive for Linux and run the hayabusa binary.

external.name: Volatility (2.x)
external.license: VSL (BSD-style); not in Debian. Superseded by Volatility 3.

why.text: The original Volatility 2 targets Python 2 and is not in Debian; use Volatility 3 unless a profile forces 2.x.

how.text: Run from the official git checkout with a Python 2 environment, per the Volatility docs.

external.name: NetworkMiner
external.summary: Passive network forensic analysis of PCAP files

why.text: NetworkMiner is closed-source .NET software and cannot be redistributed by Shadow OS.

how.text: Download the free edition from Netresec and run it under Mono/.NET on Linux.
